notes: Pump.fun bonding-curve program. 'Swap' = buy/sell against a per-mint bonding curve; executes via the wired Orquestra project's /instructions/{buy,sell}/build. Recipes from pump-fun/pump-public-docs idl/pump.json, cross-verified against real mainnet accounts. Pump tokens may be Token-2022; the ATA recipes are parameterized on token_program, which Gecko resolves from the mint owner (read_account_owner). Post-Apr-2026 program (BREAKING_FEE_RECIPIENT.md): a buy is 18 accounts — the 16 original + bonding_curve_v2 (seed ['bonding-curve-v2', mint]; created LAZILY, the ADDRESS is what the instruction needs — assert address-correct, never existence) + a buyback fee recipient from Global.buyback_fee_recipients ([pubkey;8] @ data offset 741) appended after it. fee_recipient is NOT modelled as a PDA/resolver: the live simulate Receipt established empirically that `buy` accepts a REGULAR recipient — Global.fee_recipients[0] @ data offset 162 — while the single `fee_recipient` field @ offset 41 is a BUYBACK recipient (passing it reverted 6062; earlier '@41' guidance refuted), so plan_buy declares fee_recipient as unresolved with the @162 read recipe rather than hardcode a rotatable pubkey. fee_config = PDA under the fee program pfeeUxB6...; associated_user = the trader's ATA. A `sell` is a DIFFERENT shape from a buy and the surface says so only in prose: its IDL/builder account list is 14 named accounts, it names NEITHER volume accumulator, and its doc-comment ('For cashback coins, pass as remaining_accounts: [0] user_volume_accumulator, [1] bonding_curve_v2') is the only hint. The real totals are 16 accounts for a non-cashback coin ([bonding_curve_v2 read-only, one buyback recipient writable] appended) and 17 for a cashback coin (user_volume_accumulator writable prepended to those) — BREAKING_FEE_RECIPIENT.md + @pump-fun/pump-sdk@1.36.0 getSellInstructionInternal, live-verified on four mainnet sells. The switch is BondingCurve.is_cashback_coin (bool @ data offset 82; is_mayhem_mode @ 81), so plan_sell READS it rather than asking the caller. A sell needs NO ATA prelude (the seller already holds the token) and no wSOL wrap (the curve pays native lamports).

seeds.name: creator
seeds.reason: seed is bonding_curve.data.creator — fetch the bonding_curve account + Anchor-decode its creator field; the dotted-path seed a naive IDL->derivation drops (#4057)

why.bonding_curve_v2: hidden account: required post-Apr-2026 but the IDL never names it (it travels only as a remaining_accounts entry mentioned in doc text); seed verified against pump-public-docs + mainnet
why.creator_vault: the surface honestly flags the seed (bonding_curve.creator is runtime data); the @49 read recipe that RESOLVES it came from Anchor-decoding the BondingCurve layout, not from the surface
why.associated_bonding_curve: generic ATA parameterization: the IDL binds the owner seed to the literal bonding_curve account; re-parameterized on 'owner' so one recipe serves every ATA derivation
why.associated_user: the buyer's ATA — the IDL carries no pda block for it at all; hand-modelled under the SPL Associated Token program
